header.name: Kant's Critique of Pure Reason
header.description: This course will undertake a close reading of Immanuel Kant's Critique of Pure Reason and the 'Copernican Revolution' it brought about in the epistemological sphere. The course will be held in the seminar format, with sections from the text being assigned each week, and presentations by students, followed by discussion. In addition to gaining familiarity with Kant's systematic philosophy through this canonical text, the seminar mode will provide essential training to students on how to closely engage with, and critically analyse, dense philosophical writing. Further, the course will inculcate familiarity with the scholarship and ongoing debates surrounding the text , as well as situate it in relation to other works by the author. We will take into consideration important secondary literature as a necessary supplement to the primary text. By the end of the course, students will have a detailed and comprehensive overview, not only of Kant's thought, but also how it has set the agenda for the philosophical discourse that followed.
prerequisites_desirable: Some familiarity with the basic philosophical approach/system of the philosopher in question

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Develop familiarity with the fundamental ideas in the Critique.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: analyse and criticize the text to develop reading, writing and oral skills in philosophy.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Construct a coherent, systematic interpretation of the text.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Develop the capacity to see the interconnections between the specific text and the broader philosophical tradition in which it is situated, so as to understand the historical emergence and transformation of certain philosophical issues .

Analytic of Principles: Transcendental Judgement and the Schematism of the Catgories
System of All Principles of the Pure Understanding
Overview of the arguments of the text so far
explication of what is to come in the 'Transcendental Dialectic' as the 'logic of illusion'
